findings.title: D6 overrides the architecture's config identity and widens scope beyond the effort audit
findings.description:
- The architecture defines identity as "config (alias, model, profile, effort sent)" (Design Goals, "Results stay comparable over time"). D6 drops the alias from the grouping key. It adds `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens` to identity, so it changes `ProducerConfigRef` and adds a private `config_identity` in `replay/report.py`.
- The anticipated-slice entry in the architecture is limited to: every path sends or records that it could not, and every usage record carries effort sent. Reworking replay report grouping and adding two non-effort identity fields goes past that. The slice describes itself as effort 2/5.
- D6 also states the architecture's own rule ("two rows only when the effort really differed on the wire") "already implies" the change. That is a debatable reading, because the architecture lists the alias explicitly.
- The slice rewrites an architecture-level identity rule locally and tells later slices to apply it. The architecture document is not updated.
- Cut or defer one of these:
  - Keep this slice to `effort_sent` correctness (D1–D5, D7).
  - Move the identity change to a slice that owns it, such as 424/425, where record types are defined. The architecture is amended there.
  - If D6 stays, amend the architecture's identity wording in the same change.
  - Drop `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens` unless a named requirement needs them. The slice plan criterion cited only needs rows to merge on sent effort.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/420-slice.effort-audit-across-dispatch-paths.md#D6 — Config identity is what went on the wire; the alias is display

findings.title: "Provides" guarantee overstates what the inventory delivers
findings.description:
- The slice promises "every alias-resolving dispatch path, including the grading review and the judge, sends and records effort."
- The inventory contradicts this:
  - Path 7, the findings-addressed judge, has "Records: no". It is excluded as a 175 gap.
  - Paths 10 and 11 have "no record (harness-run)".
- Downstream slices (421–427) read this as a recording guarantee. Reword it to "sends effort on all alias-resolving paths, and records it on paths 1–6, 8, 9 and 12." Name path 7 as a known gap with the issue to be filed.
- The Integration Requirement "no further effort work" has the same overreach.

findings.title: Reader raising on unrecognized stored value has no stated handling or observable signal
findings.description:
- D5 says `action_effort_sent` "raises on an unrecognized value rather than reading it as `None`." The callers are the replay outcome reader and `sq stats producers`, which scan many persisted run files.
- The slice does not say whether one corrupt or future-format record aborts the whole report or only that record, or what is logged. The project's failure-mode enumeration rule requires the failure handling to be explicit and observable.
- State the behavior at each of the two call sites. For example, fail that run's row with a WARNING that names the run id, or abort deliberately. Add one test that asserts the signal.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/420-slice.effort-audit-across-dispatch-paths.md#D5 — Effort sent is stamped on the action, not only on the usage record

findings.title: Enumeration test (D7) is reasonable but is the heaviest option for the guard
findings.description:
- The AST scan with a classification table is justified by the architecture's "precondition for effort rows meaning anything." It follows the existing SC1a pattern, so it does not need cutting.
- It is the largest single piece of test machinery in a 2/5 slice. If scope needs trimming, the per-path assertions in the Technical Requirements give most of the protection. The guard mainly covers future paths.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/420-slice.effort-audit-across-dispatch-paths.md#D7 — The inventory is enforced by an enumeration test

findings.title: Cost and latency change for the findings-addressed gate is acknowledged
findings.description:
- Sending the judge alias's effort changes the spend and latency of the pipeline gate and `sq review resolve`. The CHANGELOG bullet covers it.
- Because path 7 writes no `UsageRecord`, that change is invisible in run totals and in `pipeline.max_cost_usd`. The issue the slice plans to file should be linked from the slice before implementation.
